weakest_inference: The least-explicitly-justified step is in Section 1: from 'the gcd of the two touched p-exponents is unchanged' (gcd(min(a,b),|a-b|)=gcd(a,b), which is a correct Euclid step) the proof concludes that 'therefore the gcd of the ENTIRE multiset of p-exponents (i.e. G_p) is unchanged.' This relies on the implicit grouping identity gcd(R u {a,b}) = gcd(R u {gcd(a,b)}) = gcd(gcd(R), gcd(a,b)), i.e. full associativity of gcd over the multiset. I reconstructed this explicitly: with r=gcd of the untouched exponents, gcd(R u {a,b})=gcd(r,a,b)=gcd(r,gcd(a,b)), and the replacement a',b' satisfy gcd(a',b')=gcd(a,b), so gcd(r,gcd(a',b'))=gcd(r,gcd(a,b)). The step is therefore VALID (standard gcd associativity), not a gap; it is merely the one place a reader must fill in one line of grouping. No other inference is weaker: the move reduction (lcm/gcd=ab), the subtractive-Euclid per-prime step, DeltaT=-Omega(g), the g=1 case giving Delta c=-1, lex well-foundedness, and the final pinning v_p(M)=G_p all check out independently.
counterexample_search: Re-derived the move independently: with g=gcd(m,n), m=ga,n=gb,gcd(a,b)=1, lcm(m,n)=mn/g=gab, so lcm/gcd=gab/g=ab; move=(ga,gb)->(g,ab). Confirmed (e.g. (12,18)->(6,6); (4,6)->(2,6); (8,12)->(4,6)).

Per-prime step (alpha,beta)->(min,|alpha-beta|) verified: v_p(g)=min, v_p(ab)=(a-min)+(b-min)=|a-b|. Cross-checked that when p|n but p-|-m (alpha=0<beta), the step (0,beta)->(0,beta) leaves that prime's pair literally unchanged, so the invariant trivially holds.

Reversed both inequality implications in termination: (i) g>1 => Omega(g)>=1 => DeltaT=-Omega(g)<=-1<0, so (T,c) falls in the FIRST coordinate regardless of c (no need to bound Delta c, and indeed c never increases since two >1 entries are removed and at most two >1 entries are added). (ii) g=1 => outputs (1,mn) with exactly one outgoing entry >1, so Delta c=-1 and DeltaT=0; lexicographically (T,c)->(T,c-1). Both branches force a strict lex decrease; no third branch exists (g is a positive integer, either 1 or >1).

Existence/nonzero tested for 'exactly one >1': assumed terminal c=0 (all entries 1 => every v_p=0 => G_p=0 for all p). Invariance forces G_p=0 initially => no prime divides any a_i => all a_i=1, contradicting a_i>1. Strengthened form: any a_i>1 has a prime divisor p0 with G_p0>=1 forever, so at termination some entry carries a positive p0-valuation and is >1. Contradiction is genuine, not circular (invariant proved in Sec 1 independently of termination).

Sought a counterexample to the closed form M=prod_p p^{gcd_i v_p(a_i)} via exhaustive ALL-orderings DFS on 20000 random multisets (N=2..5, values<=20): 0 value mismatches, 0 terminal states failing 'exactly one >1'. Edge multisets all matched: {4,6}->6, {4,8}->2, {6,10,15}->30, {2,4,8,16}->2, {16,81}->1296, {12,18}->6, {8,12}->6, {2,4,9}->18, {4,4}->4, {2,3}->6.

Independently corroborated the termination pillar without leaning on DFS-bottoming-out: on 266715 random legal moves the pair (T,c) strictly decreased lexicographically 266715/266715 times (0 violations), ruling out any non-terminating play / cycle.

Checked tempting wrong answers are correctly rejected: M is neither lcm (would give {4,6}->12, actual 6) nor ordinary gcd (would give {4,6}->2; {6,10,15}->1). Candidate's falsification of these is correct.

Degenerate cases: m=n (g=m,a=b=1, outputs (m,1), DeltaT=-Omega(m)<0, c drops by 1); all entries equal; pure prime powers; coprime sets; N=1 (no move, M=a_1, consistent with formula v_p(M)=v_p(a_1)). All handled, none breaks termination or the invariant.
summary: Independent second-order audit CONFIRMS the pass. I re-derived the entire proof from scratch rather than summarizing it. Dependency graph: (move=(ga,gb)->(g,ab)) -> (per-prime subtractive-Euclid step (a,b)->(min,|a-b|), which preserves gcd(a,b)) -> (invariant G_p=gcd of all board p-valuations, using gcd-associativity to lift the pairwise preservation to the whole multiset) -> (termination via lexicographic (T,c): DeltaT=-Omega(g)<0 when g>1; DeltaT=0,Delta c=-1 when g=1; lex well-foundedness) -> (exactly one terminal entry >1 by contradiction with the invariant, since some a_i>1 forces some G_p>=1 forever) -> (M pinned by v_p(M)=G_p(initial)=gcd_i v_p(a_i), hence M=prod_p p^{gcd_i v_p(a_i)} depends only on the initial board). I attacked each link: reversed every inequality (DeltaT sign, Delta c sign in both g-cases), tested the existence/nonzero conclusion (the c=0 contradiction and the 'some G_p>=1' strengthening), checked for circularity (none: invariant is proved before termination; 'exactly one' uses termination+invariant; uniqueness uses invariant+'exactly one'), and hunted for a counterexample with exhaustive all-orderings DFS (20000 instances, 0 mismatches, 0 terminal failures) plus an independent lexicographic-decrease stress test (266715 moves, 0 violations). The single weakest inference is the implicit gcd-multiset grouping step in Section 1, but it is valid (standard associativity of gcd) and the reviewer even flagged it as a presentation-only note. No dependency gaps and no required fixes remain after the attack; both required statements (finitely many moves ending in exactly one entry M>1, and independence of M from Confucius's choices) are proved correctly, completely, rigorously, and self-containedly.
